reviews.justification: Test harnesses, vectors and generators exercise request routing, signatures and byte formats with synthetic inputs; their assertions do not award economic value to users. Current network-context, scoped-state and sponsor-projection fixtures preserve this boundary. Tests of signing or game results do not classify the production signing authority, game engines or settlement consumers as non-value. Review covers these exact files only, not future tests or live deployments.

Unsigned discovery, configuration and automation proxy inputs. No random result is used here to choose or pay an economic reward. Proxy reachability is not permission for its callers; a new final consumer requires its own classification.

Frozen reference router and chain adapter used to compare parity. They map and encode random requests but define no economic settlement. This review does not classify downstream applications as non-value.

Existing dice consumer stakes GAS and pays 5.7x on operator-predictable random.generate. The validation driver places those same wagers. This is value-bearing debt, not permission for a new integration; queued E-VRF1 must retire or replace it.

Kernel capability, routing, configuration, resource accounting and envelope definitions. These integration inputs do not consume VRF output to decide economic value; oracle service fees are independent of the random output. Caller settlement is separately classified.

Lexical matches for local deterministic game RNG state or JavaScript Math.random. These files do not call the direct, automation or oracle VRF lanes. This is an explicit reviewed false positive, not a directory exemption.

Gateway routing and retired-lane responses, including forwarding oracle fulfillment. These exact gateways define no economic payoff; final applications are separately reviewed. Generic transport alone never proves a caller non-value.

Transport, dispatch and compatibility generation for oracle results, including the unchanged sponsor projection expressed by the current config adapter. These exact adapters do not select rewards or settle wagers; final consumers require separate review, including the explicitly recorded dice debt. Forwarding is not proof that a caller is non-value.

CU-179 offline randomized-input harness for the relayer and enclave request plane. It draws every case from three committed seeds through its own xorshift32, so it holds no entropy source, and it reads no random result: the "random" it names is the router request-type label, and the oracle-random, feed, price, envelope and sponsor paths are asserted only on shapes, refusals, request-id stringification and clamp monotonicity. Its inputs are synthetic and it awards no value. This review covers this file and no other part of the CU-179 change.

CU-230 policy-binding freshness reporter and its tests. The reporter reads this policy, hashes the bytes of each bound input with node:crypto sha256, compares them with the recorded hash and prints the difference; with --base it reads the same paths at a base commit through git show to say whether the change under test caused the staleness. It holds no entropy source and consumes no random result: the only randomness-shaped strings in either file are the name of the VRF-consumer gate they report for and a marked fixture the tests use to build a repository that gate accepts. Neither file reaches a chain, wallet, database or payout, and neither awards value. This review covers these two files and no other part of the CU-230 change.

The key-free public-source price quorum behind the feed PriceSource seam: a median of at least two independent venues, an inclusive 5 percent deviation guard, and a refusal when a single source would decide a quote. It fetches unauthenticated public market data and returns price numbers to the existing feed planner; it consumes no randomness, drives no payout, and adds no new signing or settlement lane. The HTTP-boundary suite entry is the host boot refusal for an unknown FEED_PRICE_PLANE, so a typo cannot fall back to the single-source plane. None of these inputs is a VRF consumer.

Disposable private-chain acceptance for the kernel, relayer, host and custody request path and the delivery-path fixes it exercises. Private-chain settlement uses disposable local state; this review does not authorize live signing or classify downstream consumers.
